id: qc-07
title: Loophole-free Bell tests
paper: Hensen et al., Loophole-free Bell inequality violation using electron spins separated by 1.3 km (arXiv Aug 2015; Nature 526, 682, 2015)
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.05949
type: Replication
cutoff: 2015-08-24
domain: qc
profile: observation

## expected_verdict
Supported (strong) with a recorded common-mode dependency. The violation itself is modest (p = 0.039, 245 trials). Two independent photonic groups replicated it with much stronger statistics. All three share the ICFO random-number generators for setting choice, which must be noted when assigning the tier.

## I0
Can a separated entangled system violate a Bell inequality with key loopholes closed?

## evidence
- Setup: NV-centre electron spins in diamond at labs A and B, 1.3 km apart; event-ready entanglement swapping (Barrett–Kok) at location C; fast quantum RNG basis choice; single-shot spin readout.
- Loopholes addressed: detection (efficient readout, no fair sampling), locality (space-like separation of setting choice and readout), plus fast random basis selection.
- Result: 245 trials, CHSH S = 2.42 ± 0.20; null-hypothesis test p = 0.039 for a local-realist model ("complete" analysis allowing arbitrary memory in the devices; a stronger value is obtained if trials are assumed i.i.d.).
- Quantum prediction S = 2√2 ≈ 2.83; local bound S ≤ 2.
- RNGs supplied by ICFO co-authors (Abellán, Amaya, Pruneri, Mitchell).

## intake
- Scope: a Bell (CHSH) violation with detection and locality loopholes closed simultaneously.
- Regime: 1.3 km separation; event-ready heralding; 245 trials over the run.
- Assumptions: setting choices are free / unpredictable (RNG quality); no hidden communication within space-like intervals; statistical test valid under memory effects.
- Falsifiers: a timing analysis showing settings not space-like separated; RNG predictability; p-value not robust to the test choice.

## screen
- Must flag: small sample (245 trials) and p = 0.039 is weak evidence alone; the freedom-of-choice assumption rests on the RNGs; this is a foundations result, not a computational advantage.
- Must not reject it for being "only" p = 0.039 when independent replications exist.

## retrieval
- Pre-cutoff must-finds: Bell 1964; CHSH 1969; Aspect et al. 1982 (locality); Weihs et al. 1998; Giustina et al. 2013 / Christensen et al. 2013 (detection loophole); Bernien et al. 2013 heralded NV entanglement.
- Current mode: Giustina et al. 2015 (photons, p = 3.74×10⁻³¹, 11.5σ) and Shalm et al. 2015 (photons, p down to 5.9×10⁻⁹; 2.3×10⁻⁷ adjusted for RNG predictability). Both share the ICFO RNG suppliers.

## designer
- Pre-specify event selection, timing windows, the setting-generation scheme and the hypothesis test before data inspection; plan a sample size giving p < 10⁻³.

## champion
- The local-realist bound S ≤ 2 under the stated assumptions (the null model); no classical algorithm comparator.

## panel
- Accept. Request (a) the space-time diagram confirming separation, (b) RNG independence analysis, (c) a note on the shared RNG component across replications.

## run
- If trial-level data are public: recompute S and the p-value from 245 trials. Otherwise recompute S = 2.42 from reported correlators; hardware BLOCKED.

## verdict
- Label: Supported (strong) across three experiments; tier noting common-mode RNG dependency.
- Must say: independent platforms (spins, photons) and groups replicate; shared RNG supply is a dependency.
- Must not say: this paper alone is decisive at high significance; or it demonstrates quantum computational advantage.

## audit
- Check: 1.3 km; 245 trials; S = 2.42 ± 0.20; p = 0.039; replication p-values; ICFO authors on all three papers.

## variants
- Replication with independently implemented setting generation (e.g. cosmic or human-choice RNGs) to remove the common-mode dependency.
